The learned Advocate then submits that there being materials to indicate that opposite party Nos. 1 to 3, the process servers, served summons improperly and accused opposite party No. 4 being witness to the aforesaid service return the impugned order should be knocked down. Elaborating the submissions he submits that as a result of fraudulent service of summons upon the defendants the suit has been decreed against the petitioner and the opposite party Nos. 1-3 submitted a false service return and the opposite party No. 4 attested it and they ought not to have been discharged. 

 5. Mr Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 to 4, submits that Chapter XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure is applicable in case of trial of cases under Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 (Act XL of 1958). He then submits that under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure contained in Chapter XX of the Code, the Court is obliged to consider the case record and the documents sent therewith. He then refers to the First Information Report and the charge-sheet and submits that in the four corners of the First Information Report or charge-sheet there is no allegation whatsoever in so many words that the accused opposite parties did anything as to suppression of summons resulting in the decree of Title Suit No. 472 of 1981 and that it is not understood whether the process servers served any summons and, if so, upon whom. He further submits that in the absence of any other materials before the learned Judge disclosing commission of any offence by the accused opposite parties there was no reason to presume that the accused opposite parties committed any offence as alleged and, as such, the learned Judge on consideration of the case record and the documents submitted therewith passed the impugned order which does not suffer from any illegality. He then submits that it has been alleged in the revisional application that the accused opposite parties committed offence punishable under sections 417/420/467/471/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 by forging and fabricating papers that resulted in obtaining ex parte decree from the Court by suppressing the summons. The learned Advocate then refers to section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and submits that the offence alleged if any has been committed in relation to the proceeding of Title Suit No. 472 of 1981 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge and, as such, except a complaint of the said Court no Court can take cognizance of such offence. Elaborating further the point, the learned Advocate submits that in view of the bar of section 195 of the Code no proceeding should be allowed to continue against the accused opposite parties and in this view of the matter also the order of discharge passed by the learned Judge cannot be found fault with. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner found it difficult to reply to this submission of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties. We have also given our anxious consideration to this aspect of the case and we are in agreement with the views expressed by the learned Advocate of the opposite parties 1-4 and hold that the offences alleged to have been committed in connection with proceeding of a Civil Court cannot be tried by any other Court except upon a complaint by the said Court. 

 6. We have considered other submissions made at the Bar and perused the materials on record. On perusal of the first information report it is not clear as to what role, if any, has been played by the accused opposite party Nos. 1-4 in obtaining the decree in question. Similarly, in the charge sheet also there is no such material disclosed against the accused opposite party Nos.1 to 4 as to their role played in the commission of the alleged offence. None of the parties produced statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before us to examine whether, in fact, there were any other materials against the accused opposite party No. 1 to 4. It does not appear from the impugned order that the learned Judge also had any occasion to peruse the said statements. In the absence of any material disclosing any offence alleged to have been committed by the accused opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 the impugned order discharging them from the charge, in our view, does not call for interference.
